note: AN UPLOADED LOGO DOES NOT INVERT - and the mechanism was never what was missing. OPTION A, THE PLATE, CHOSEN, because this codebase had already chosen it: .logo-plate has been in globals.css since theming stage 3 with a docblock weighing a plate against a second per-tenant dark upload (asks the church for a file most will not have, and a missing one must fall back) and a computed filter (automatic, and it mangles a coloured logo). What was open was COVERAGE: TEN surfaces render a tenant-uploaded logo and exactly TWO carried the class - MainApp's desktop rail and AuthPage. EIGHT were bare, and seven of them are the PUBLIC giving and registration pages a stranger opens from a shared link: /giving, /pledge, /campaign, /event, /checkin, /form and /calendar. None is in PREAUTH_PATHS, so unlike /auth and /onboarding they are not forced light - they follow the visitor's prefers-color-scheme and paint --surface-tint, #141414 in dark. MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: the shipped PublicGiving is rendered from source into a real Chromium with the real compiled stylesheet, and near-black ink (#1A1A1A) on the plate measures 16.42:1 while the same mark with the class stripped off that same element measures 1.06:1 on the page ground - a factor of 15.5, not a rounding error. 1.06:1 is not 'a bit low': it is invisible. THE NINTH SURFACE WAS FOUND BY THE SWEEP: AIChat's empty state, whose own comment says it matches MainApp/AuthPage, both of which plate. THE TENTH, AdminDashboard's desktop rail mark, IS SPLIT OUT WITH THE COST MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED: the one-class change was made, the full suite was run, and it reddened TWELVE suites plus THE-305 - AdminDashboard.tsx is digest-frozen by THIRTEEN separate freeze registers, each keeping its own accepted list. Every one has a documented append path, so the change is possible; it is disproportionate. Thirteen freeze registers edited for one 36px mark on a screen the church's own administrator opens, against seven PUBLIC pages a stranger opens from a shared link, is the wrong trade in one PR, and a wrong digest in a freeze register is worse than no change. The split is ASSERTED, not just described: the guard fails if a later ticket plates that file without taking it out of SPLIT_OUT_SURFACES, so the exemption cannot outlive its reason. THE PLATE COSTS NOTHING IN LIGHT: it paints no background and no ring there, and because it is drawn with box-shadow rather than padding the logo's box is identical with and without the class in BOTH themes - so a transparent logo that needed no plate is not boxed and is not moved. THE SMALLER HALF, THE CLIENT-SIDE ACCENT DESYNC, IS ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED - IN A NEW MODULE, BECAUSE theme.ts IS BYTE-FROZEN: appending the helper to theme.ts was tried and reddened the-271-one-theme-system and posthog-untouched, which pin it deliberately as the shared theme vocabulary, so src/lib/brand-accent.ts COMPOSES its exports instead and theme.ts is byte-identical to main. layout.tsx stamps --brand-color, --brand-color-on-dark and --brand-color-on-tint together from one hex, but two client paths wrote only the first, through documentElement.style.setProperty - an INLINE style on <html>, which beats the server's :root block on specificity. So the raw accent moved while the two DERIVED properties kept the value the server computed from the PREVIOUS hex, and every on-dark consumer painted an accent corrected against a colour no longer on screen. In TenantContext that is brief; in BrandingSection's live colour picker it persists for as long as the admin is on the screen, which is precisely when they are judging the colour. Both now go through applyBrandAccent, which writes all three or none - a malformed hex writes NOTHING, because deriveOnDarkAccent returns its input unchanged for anything it cannot parse and writing on that would replace a correct derived accent with a broken one. The property set is DERIVED from layout.tsx by reading it, never by restating it, so the two cannot drift and layout.tsx is not touched. NOTHING WAS RE-LITIGATED: --chart-4 (1.50:1), --chart-5 (1.77:1), progress (2.30:1) and the 4.77:1 worst text pair are ACCEPTED and already pinned in three other suites; 'improving' --chart-4 was run as a mutation and reddened three of them, so they are verified rather than duplicated a fourth time. NO NEW TOKEN, NO NEW COMPONENT, NO NEW DEPENDENCY. NO firestore.rules DIGEST IS RECORDED HERE and that is a finding rather than an omission: this ticket adds no Firestore operation of any kind - it changes a class name on eight img elements and the set of custom properties two client paths write - so there is nothing a rule could express. TWO PRE-EXISTING FINDINGS ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN FIXED: PublicCheckin greets an arriving member with a pictographic emoji in user-facing text, against the house rule, and PublicEventRegistration carries a typographic check mark; both predate this ticket and deleting deliberate copy off a public screen is not this ticket's mandate, so the first is pinned by content so a SECOND one still fails. EVERY GUARD HERE WAS VERIFIED BY MUTATION - strip the plate from the measured surface, strip it from a different surface so only the sweep can catch it, kill the mechanism in CSS with the markup left intact, revert each half of the accent fix - and every one failed before being restored.

NO READ, NO WRITE, NO GATE, NO ENDPOINT, NO CONTROL AND NO STRING MOVED in this file; the form, the copy, the fallback wordmark for a tenant with no logo at all, and every other element are untouched.
